title: precommit's six two-way guards name exit codes their branch never reads
body:
## What happens

`bin/.devbin/cmd/precommit` reads six guards two ways, `if ! bash "$TOOLS/<guard>"`, and each one's failure line names its cause by an exit code that the branch never reads: `corrected_check.sh` and `class_vocab_check.sh` ("exit 2; its findings never gate"), `machine_table_check.sh` ("exit 2"), and `declared_kind_check.sh`, `absent_at_check.sh` and `rulings_check.sh` ("exit 1", or "exit 2"). Any non-zero exit takes the branch, so a missing tool's 127, bash's 126 or the tool's own die() is reported as the cause the label names. That is the class issue 0714 fixed for three guards.

## The fix

Each of the six runs as `x=0; bash <tool> || x=$?` and is read through issue 0720's `guard_verdict`, so its failure line names only what its status established: its own finding text where its status is the finding its tool defines, and the one no-verdict wording otherwise. Where a tool gives an exit code a meaning of its own, eg a measurement that never gates, that meaning is read by name, never by the branch.

Found by devbin-dc's Highlander sweep for issue 0720 (2026-11-20). It rides this release (hv decision 69).
